description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/ref.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  1 blessed row.  A WRONG DIAGNOSIS, not a missing
one -- both perl and PCL die, and only the message differs.

PROBED (scratch/s473t6a/probes/misc1.pl E1, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 2ac855aa):

    eval { ()[0]{foo} };

    perl: Can't use an undefined value as a HASH reference
    PCL : Modification of a read-only value attempted

t/op/ref.t line 675 asserts perl's text with `like`, so the row fails.

The PCL message is the AUTOVIVIFICATION path's: an element access on an
undefined slice result is treated as an lvalue and the write is refused,
where perl asks the KIND question first.  The row is the one place the two
orders are distinguishable, and it is cheap only if the deref path already
knows it is in RVALUE position -- which is the same information #1241 and
#1663 need for the vivification rule, so read those first.

USER standing: exact fatal-error TEXT is not a goal unless cheap.  What makes
this one worth a task rather than a `NS:Error message text and format` row is
that PCL is raising the WRONG KIND of error, not a differently-worded one.
subject: ()[0]{foo} dies "Modification of a read-only value attempted" where perl says "Can't use an undefined value as a HASH reference" -- the wrong KIND of error, not wrong wording
